context:
Goal: every pull request gets the review depth its kind of change needs, set by one table, with no gap where two rules disagree.
Problem (rule): the round rules list names the checks inside merge/ but not every file there, so the table cell for the merge tool is unset and only you can say which files count.
Based on (read): the plan plan on branch lane/pr-template-risk-tiers (docs/plans/pr-template-risk-tiers.md, read from main commit 69ab998832, 21:38 CST Nov 17): the list names merge/ checks, not all of merge/.
Departs from: main — the list names merge/ checks only and no decision covers the rest of merge/ — a reading is picked (a or b).
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; step pr-template-risk-tiers waits on your pick, then a test-author writes the template-check cases and a builder lands them.

options.gain: Matches the list; no new cost on routine merge-tool edits.
options.how: The table follows the list as written. Round 1 stays Haiku at xhigh, as for every change.
options.label: Only the merge/ check files count: the net-value test applies there, not to other merge/ files (recommended)
options.lose: An edit to a merge/ file that is not a listed check owes no net-value test.

options.gain: The merge tool, which every merge depends on, always gets the net-value test.
options.how: The table row reads guard or check yes for any merge/ file. Round 1 stays Haiku at xhigh, as for every change.
options.label: All of merge/ counts: the net-value test applies to any merge/ edit that fails its last round
options.lose: More review work on every merge-tool edit that fails a round.

ref: owner chat 19:45 CST Nov 17 (relayed by the consultant): land the verification article's findings; PR template lines and risk tiers by change
reply: Fastest while still effective is a (only the merge/ check files count). One correction to the item: the 'stronger first review' wording is wrong. Round 1 runs the same model (Haiku at xhigh) for every change, a guard or check change included (your ruling of 19:45 CST Nov 17, decision agent-model-cap). I removed my claim that the label changes only what is owed after a failed round (a net-value test and a third round). That was my reading, not your ruling, and it is not written in any rule file on main. What the label does change is in your rule roles-review-cap-three (global CLAUDE.md): a round that passes ends review, a guard or check change included; the net-value test runs only when a guard or check change reaches round 3, after a round 2 FAIL with no passing fix verifier, or a round 1 FAIL whose fix verifiers all FAIL; a change with no guard or check skips the test. So the label never by itself calls for a third round. I have asked the consultant for its view and will add it here. Item 956 has the same wrong wording.
short: Tier table: which merge-tool files count as checks?

shown.label: Only the merge/ check files count: the net-value test applies there, not to other merge/ files (recommended)
All of merge/ counts: the net-value test applies to any merge/ edit that fails its last round

title: Which files under merge/ make a pull request a guard or check change?
why: a matches the list as written; b is safer but adds the net-value test to every merge-tool edit. Round 1 is the same model either way (decision agent-model-cap). Recommended by triage, not owner-typed.
